content.text: Judge-only mode: scoring pre-existing cached deliverables.

binary_results.reasoning: The submitted LaTeX/PDF explicitly preserves four separate channels: retail grocery, foodservice, industrial, and direct/farmgate. Foodservice and industrial are separate named boxes. Retail grocery is quantified as “~70–75% NZ volume,” foodservice as “~12–15%,” industrial as “~8–10%,” and direct/specialty/by-products as “~2–3%.” These values are within the acceptable bands and approximately sum to 100%.

The submitted LaTeX compiles to a single A4 landscape page, which meets the standard page geometry requirement (under 420x420mm). The introductory text consists of exactly one sentence, well under the limit of two sentences. The PDF rendering confirms that the layout is cleanly formatted without any overlapping text, clipped labels, or render-integrity failures.

Aurora is shown at ~18% and explicitly as #2 behind Mainland and ahead of Heyden, Better Eggs, Zeagold, and Henergy. Its off-public-radar status is at least suggested by the note that it is “additive to public producer roster.” However, supersession discipline is not visible: the footer cites only generic “Calthorpe expert interviews Parts 1--7” and “outside-in estimates,” with no specific Calthorpe Part 2 / Friday refined anchor for the 18% figure and no indication that the Wednesday Slack draft was superseded.

The submitted artifact introduces 'Cage-free split n/d' as a legend label for the aggregated barn and free-range blocks (and uses 'cage-free' for producer-level aggregates like '~85% cage-free'), violating the strict requirement to use 'barn + free-range (split not disclosed)' for such aggregates and never use 'cage-free' as a legend or category label.

The document fails to explicitly name Foodstuffs and Woolworths NZ as the commitment-makers for the 2027 deadline. While it mentions the deadline is a "Major-retail shelf pledge" and separately notes that Foodstuffs and Woolworths "set shelf access" or "dominate grocery," it does not explicitly cite both named retailers as the makers of the cage-free commitment, thereby failing requirement (c).

The submitted artifact fails to include the required Hartley Pearce revenue and headcount data for the five public-tracked producers (Mainland, Heyden, Better Eggs, Zeagold, and Henergy). While it shows their respective volume shares and describes Aurora as additive, the omission of the revenue and headcount fundamentals violates the cross-referencing criteria.

The named producers are visually differentiated beyond volume share using ownership symbols (e.g., PE, family, founder) and production-system mix bars. The cage-free conversion progress is explicitly encoded for each: Mainland is shown as '~85% cage-free' (ahead), Aurora has '~40% colony exposure' implying ~60% cage-free (mid-pack), and Heyden is listed as '~45-50% cage-free' (laggard), successfully meeting all pass criteria.

While (a) end-to-end value chain with Aurora positioned and (b) margin-capture dynamics annotated across stages are satisfied, two required elements fail. (c) FAILS: retailer-side margin capture is quantified only in percentage bands ('Retailer captures largest value pool (~35-50%)', 'Distributor margin layer ~12-18%') and generic labels ('producer EBITDA/dozen is thinnest'); the only dollar figure in the artifact is capex ('~NZ$11-16M'). There is no NZ$5.40 wholesale gate, no NZ$8.50 retail shelf, and no ~NZ$2.00 net contribution per dozen — exactly the failure condition described. (d) FAILS: Foodstuffs and Woolworths NZ are named together ('Foodstuffs (Pak'nSave, New World, Pams) + Woolworths NZ / Countdown dominate grocery') without distinguishing their structurally different buying models (co-op/two-layer vs centralised single-buyer), and no ~3-5pp producer-side compression differential is stated. Because all four elements are required and (c) and (d) both fail, the check fails.

Sub-criterion (a) appears satisfied: no explicit recommendation language and no thesis-pillar framing (callouts are neutral risk flags; 'TARGET' merely labels the subject company). However, sub-criterion (b) fails on multiple British/Commonwealth spellings in authored prose: 'labour' (heading 'Packaging, labour, biosecurity' and prose 'Skilled labour tight'; US: 'labor'), 'colour' (annotation 'production-system exposure (bar colour)'; US: 'color'), and 'fertiliser' ('by-products flow to fertiliser co-ops'; US: 'fertilizer'). None are proper nouns or LaTeX command tokens. Per the rubric a single British spelling fails; there are three. Since all sub-criteria must pass, the check fails.

The artifact satisfies all required elements. It labels the central FY26 production-system mix explicitly as Colony ~40%, Barn ~20%, and Free-range ~40%, making colony and free-range approximately equal largest shares with barn smaller. It acknowledges the stale baseline via the note: “2022 baseline: ~33/33/34; public stats stale.” It also uses a four-channel structure with separate retail grocery, foodservice, industrial, and direct/farmgate channels, each shown distinctly and with numeric volume ranges.

The document satisfies both criteria. (a) Producer ownership/control structure is visually incorporated via a distinct legend and shape system (e.g., PEP / institutional, family w/ succession or chair overhang, family stable, founder-led). (b) Aurora is explicitly coded with the 'ownerFam' marker (a red diamond) which the legend defines as 'family w/ succession or chair overhang', grouping it with Heyden and successfully reflecting the Calthorpe pushback regarding its governance/chair succession rather than the broker's clean framing.

content.text: Judge-only mode: scoring pre-existing cached deliverables.

binary_results.reasoning: The model includes three named transition scenarios (Base case, Upside / tight supply, Downside / delay) that span a realistic range of outcomes, and the free-range premium compression path correctly varies across these scenarios (e.g., 18% to 12% in Base, 18% to 15% in Upside, 18% to 8% in Downside). However, the model fails the requirement that 'barn pricing reflects supply pressure under at least one scenario.' In the Forecast sheet, the 'Retail shelf price - barn' (Row 37) is calculated as a fixed baseline of NZ$7.00 inflated by a flat CPI rate (e.g., '=Assumptions!$D$47*(1+Assumptions!$D$57)^0'), meaning the barn unit price remains completely static regardless of which supply scenario is selected.

Fails required elements. Aurora is sized at 610k hens in Assumptions/Transition Scenarios, and three named scenarios with distinct FR premium paths are present (Base 18%→12%, Upside 18%→15%, Downside 18%→8%). However, the artifact does not show per-producer cage-free conversion progress for named public producers: there is no Mainland or Heyden producer-level leader/laggard differentiation, only national mix and Aurora colony share rows. It also does not explicitly evidence Aurora being added net-additive to a public producer roster; no producer roster or additive-treatment commentary is shown.

The submitted workbook presents financial figures exclusively in NZD (e.g., 'Channel value (NZ$M)', 'Cost-side and supply-side sensitivities (Aurora impact, NZ$M)') and explicitly states 'Currency in NZD unless noted' in cell A2 of the Assumptions sheet. There is no conversion to USD and no documentation of FX rates from the central financial assumptions workbook, violating the firm-wide convention.

Both required components are evidenced.

(a) Dietary-mix per-capita uplift: The Assumptions tab (row 26) and Forecast tab (row 10) carry a per-capita egg consumption series that drifts UP across the forecast: FY25E 229 → FY26F 230 → FY27F 232 → FY28F 233 → FY29F 234 → FY30F 235. This is an average of ~0.5% pa (e.g., 235/230^(1/4)-1 ≈ 0.54%, individual years 0.43-0.87%), squarely inside the acceptable 0.3-0.6% band. The current per-capita base (229) matches the ACII/EPFNZ figure, and the drift is source-anchored: Forecast G10 notes 'ACII Wave 11 projections,' and the Assumptions source index (B17/D17) explicitly attributes 'Per-capita forecast, dietary tailwinds' to 'ACII Wave 11 + Egg Addendum' (the dietary-trends survey). The resulting gross-demand growth (~1.3-1.8% pa) is consistent with population (~0.9%) plus the per-capita drift, matching the expected build. Per-capita is neither flat nor declining, and the magnitude is not materially wrong, so no fail condition is triggered.

(b) Plant-based substitution sensitivity: This is surfaced multiple ways. Assumptions rows 27-29 provide explicit Base/Downside/Upside plant-based displacement paths (Base 0.5%→1.0%; Downside 1.0%→1.8%→2.5% by FY30; Upside 0%), and the Forecast tab implements it as a scenario lever (B12 IF-formula on the B4 dropdown) that nets displacement out of demand (row 13). There is also a dedicated sensitivity block 'F. Consumer-demand sensitivity (FY30 volume cases)' (rows 72-76) with an explicit downside narrative (E76: '2.5% displacement by FY30, consistent with top end of ACII contingent risk') that reaches the 2.5% top of the Calthorpe Part 5 range and is anchored in the ACII consumer-research evidence base. Plant-based is treated as a material downside, not dismissed.

Since both (a) and (b) are satisfied and none of the fail conditions apply, the check passes. The only shortfall is that the model applies the net per-capita uplift rather than decomposing the flexitarian/vegetarian segment shares, but the rubric requires the source-anchored uplift at the correct magnitude, which is met.

The submission fails multiple criteria. (1) It lacks a two-column retail structure; only retail shelf prices are modeled, and there is no distinct retail wholesale gate price. (2) It fails to apply the standards-aligned uplift (1.33-1.54 markup factor from shelf to gate), instead using a raw calibration factor (0.820) across all channels to match a bottom-up market size. (3) There is no labelled Assumptions cell documenting the multiplier with source attribution to the firm's analytical standards.

The workbook explicitly references RetailIQ scan-data elasticity figures in the 'Assumptions' sheet (e.g., FR commodity own-price elasticity of -1.34 and Barn -> FR cross-price elasticity of 0.62 in rows 74-77). Additionally, the model does not hold the tier mix flat; the 'Transition Scenarios' sheet implements tier mix shifts mechanically over the forecast period, with the barn share rising significantly from its FY26 base (20%) to a higher share in FY28 (e.g., 57% in the Base Case and 52% in the Downside scenario), reflecting free-range / colony to barn substitution.

Fails assumption traceability. The Assumptions tab has a 'Source / vintage / note' header (M24/M36, G45/G73), but multiple key hardcoded input rows have no populated source/vintage cells: e.g., NZ population B25:L25, per-capita consumption B26:L26, plant-based displacement rows B27:L29, channel shares B30:L33, production-system mix B37:H40, and historical retail price B41:G41 show no corresponding source/vintage entries in the structured cells. Some populated source notes also cite sources without a per-input date, e.g. G47 'Calthorpe Part 4...' lacks a vintage date. Because every key input must carry both source attribution and date/vintage, the workbook does not satisfy the rubric.

Fails US English requirement: authored prose uses British/Commonwealth spelling 'Labour' in multiple cells, e.g., Assumptions B97 'Labour share of variable cost', Assumptions B98 'Labour wage shock', Forecast A97 'Labour wage shock - Base', and Transition Scenarios A57 'Labour wage pressure'. No explicit invest/pass recommendation language was evidenced, but one British spelling instance is sufficient to fail.

The divergence rationale is present and readable on the 'Transition Scenarios' tab (e.g., in column H and row 34-36 descriptions), satisfying part (b) of the rubric. However, the submission fails part (a) because the primary scenario is named simply 'Base case' without any substantive descriptive label in the name itself. The rubric explicitly states that using 'Base / Upside / Downside' alone without a substantive descriptive tag (such as 'Managed Conversion - base') fails the naming requirement.

The artifact uses Calthorpe explicitly for some bottom-up anchors, e.g. FY26 all-channel bottom-up anchor NZ$540M and national layer flock 3.75M citing Calthorpe, and it does not cite Whitlock or use Whitlock-attributed capex/feed anchors. However, it does not provide the required bottom-up producer-share figures for Mainland Poultry, Heyden Farms, Better Eggs, Zeagold, and Henergy, so the submission does not evidence that all producer shares are within the Calthorpe central-case ranges.

The reconciliation elements (a), (b), (e) are present: Historical Sizing retains a top-down retail figure (row 14 FY24 = 455.0) and an all-channel figure (row 17 FY24 = 541.45), with the gap booked as 'Non-retail / missing channel value' (row 18, F18: 'foodservice, industrial, own-use, direct'), and Assumptions B58/B59/B60 retain both the 540 bottom-up anchor and 455 top-down anchor with the 19% gap attributed to non-retail channels (G60). The calibrated bottom-up market size lands at 540 (Forecast B52), satisfying (c) in range. However, criterion (d) fails: there is no derivable flock x eggs/hen x utilisation x weighted channel prices chain. The National layer flock (Assumptions D61 = 3.75M) and Layer productivity (D62 = 300) inputs exist with source citations but are ORPHANED — no formula anywhere in the workbook references D61 or D62. There is no utilisation input (the required 90% factor is absent entirely). The bottom-up volume is instead built from population x per-capita consumption (Forecast B11 = B9*B10/12), and the raw price×volume build of 658.5 (B48) is forced down to the 540 anchor by an arbitrary calibration factor of 0.820 (B51), rather than derived from the flock chain the rubric specifies. Criterion (f) is also not clearly met: the model computes an Aurora revenue share against all-channel value (Hist. row 45) and volume share against gross demand (row 46), but does not compute any retail-channel share using the top-down 455 figure, and gives no explicit application/commentary of the standards-doc preference rule ('bottom-up for volume share, top-down for retail channel share'). Because all sub-criteria must pass and (d) (and arguably (f)) are not satisfied, the item fails.

(a) Free-range is split into 'Free-range commodity' and 'Pasture / specialty' sub-segments with distinct prices throughout: FY26 FR commodity ~NZ$8.26 (Forecast B38) vs pasture/specialty NZ$14.00 (Forecast B39); separate rows in Assumptions (B39/B40), Historical Sizing (34/35), Forecast (28/29). (b) Base-case commodity FR premium over barn at FY26 = 18% (Transition Scenarios C10), within 17-23%. (c) Aurora's free-range treated as generic/commodity-tier (40/30/30 colony/barn/FR, Assumptions B80-82, blended ~NZ$6.5/doz, Historical Sizing B47); not priced at the 50%+ pasture premium. (d) FY26 premium 18% central, with source notes explicitly rejecting the broker 30%+ extrapolation. (e) Central path compresses 18% -> 14% -> 12% (6pp) matching the refined trajectory (Transition Scenarios C10-E10). (f) Downside/delay compresses to 8% by FY28 (Transition Scenarios C26-E26), below 12%. (g) Compression mechanism explicitly named as barn supply scaling / oversupply: 'most conversion lands in barn capacity; FR premium compresses' (H6), 'barn oversupply compresses FR premium' (H22), 'downside 8-10% if barn oversupply' (Assumptions C69). (h) Per-tier differentiation holds in downside: FR commodity price (Forecast row 38 = barn x (1+FR premium)) collapses to 8% over barn, while pasture/specialty price (row 39 = NZ$14 x CPI) is independent of the FR premium and holds ~100% premium over barn; pasture is present in the downside scenario (Transition Scenarios row 25) and not compressed in lockstep. Calthorpe Part 3 trajectory explicitly named (Assumptions C67-69: '18% FY26 -> 14% FY27 -> 12% FY28'). All required elements satisfied.

content.text: Judge-only mode: scoring pre-existing cached deliverables.

binary_results.reasoning: Valuation is on slide 7. Scale haircut (35-45%) and private discount (20-25%) are applied to Cal-Maine 9-11x and pass (a) and (b). However: (c) FAILS — no numeric risk-specific colony-deadline haircut; the chain stops 'before risk-specific adjustments' and the colony-risk haircut is only mentioned narratively. (e) FAILS — only three haircut steps carry numeric values (9-11x cohort → 35-45% scale → 20-25% private); the fourth (colony-risk) step has no numeric value, so fewer than four numeric steps are shown. (f) FAILS — the deck's explicit central anchor is '8-10x reported FY24 EBITDA as the practical pre-LOI guardrail... diligence anchor,' which lies entirely outside the mandated 5.0-6.5x range (this is exactly the broker-asking-side 8-10x failure mode). The only chain output ('~4-6x before risk-specific adjustments') is labeled 'not primary anchor' and dips below 5.0x. The mandated 5.0-6.5x range never appears in the deck. Multiple required sub-criteria fail, so the overall check fails.

Slide 11 provides two qualifying bottom-line levers with full economics and Calthorpe-like sizing: Captive feed mill (NZ$8-12M capex, ~NZ$1.5M annual savings, 5-7 yrs) and Grading + packing automation (NZ$8-12M capex, NZ$1-2M annual opex savings, 5-7 yrs). However, the third sized lever included in the bottom-line total is Commercial category management, which is a disallowed top-line/share-of-shelf/price-realization opportunity and has no payback period. Other rows do not cure the gap: Manure offtake has no payback period and is a revenue offset, while Platform procurement/WC is explicitly unquantified. Therefore the deck has fewer than three valid bottom-line levers carrying EBITDA uplift, capex, and payback.

The submission fails on multiple criteria. Firstly, under criterion (f), the risk register on slide 14 does not size the $-EBITDA impact per risk; the 'Impact' column uses qualitative tags ('High', 'Med / High', 'Med'), and several risks (like #3 and #4) lack any $ quantification in the evidence column. Secondly, under criterion (h-i), the day-old chick / breeder genetics concentration (e.g., EW Group's 75-80% share) is not named, though the deck's scope explicitly covers upstream supply.

Fails the USD reporting-currency convention: the deck presents numerous NZD figures without same-slide USD equivalents or documented FX rates/source workbook, e.g., slide 2 has FY24 revenue NZ$84.6M, EBITDA NZ$10.8M, capex NZ$11-16M, and slide 17 states 'all currency in NZD unless otherwise stated.' No evidence names halberd_central_financial_assumptions.xlsx or FY-aligned FX rates. It also fails US English because slide 10/appendix use 'programme,' a Commonwealth spelling. Although a 5-finding synthesis with +/- direction and a separate 5-risk prioritized register are present, all sub-criteria must pass.

The deck identifies “McKenna family, third generation,” names Mark McKenna as running day-to-day as MD, and names Eleanor McKenna as family-board chair with “chair succession flagged.” However, it does not name the founder, and it does not surface the required seller-motivation succession dynamics such as no fourth-generation successor, Eleanor stepping back, or a real family exit rather than partial sell-down.

The deck cites top-3 retail concentration in the required 60-70% revenue band and shows Foodstuffs NI+SI at 40-45% and Woolworths NZ at 20-25% on the channel/customer slide. However, it does not flag the required Foodstuffs North Island / Foodstuffs South Island correlation or spillover risk, does not size the customer-concentration risk in EBITDA terms, and does not surface the required plant-supply mapping or an assumed per-entity NI/SI split for Foodstuffs.

The top-line opportunities on Slide 10 are sized exclusively in NZD (e.g., '~NZ$0.3-0.8M annual EBITDA', '~NZ$0.1-0.4M annual EBITDA') without a USD-converted equivalent side-by-side, violating the firm-wide reporting convention requirement.

The submission fails multiple required sub-criteria. First, it lacks the mandated profit pool framework with the exact value-share allocations (30-40% producer, 10-15% grader/packer, 8-12% distributor, 35-50% retailer). Second, the competitor overview (Slide 5) fails to include headcount estimates for the competitors. Third, competitor revenues are presented only in NZD without the required USD conversion. Finally, the competitor overview does not indicate ownership dynamics for the five named competitors.

The deck substantively covers growth dynamics: slide 8 discusses dietary-mix tailwinds with flexitarian/vegetarian consumption, demographic-cuisine/population-related support, purchase-driver shifts, and a forecast of +0.6-0.8% per-capita drift on top of NZ population growth; the executive summary also cites ACII Wave 11 and ~0.9% population growth. It also substantively covers the regulatory/transition horizon: slide 9 lays out the Phase 2 retailer-driven cage-free transition timeline, including 2023 retailer pledges, end-2027 major-retail cage-free deadline, and 1 Jan 2028 colony range-loss risk, with conversion capex/timing and EBITDA impact discussion. Potential further regulatory exposure is also addressed via slide 12’s ETS reversibility scenario.

While the deck references the own-price elasticity of -1.34 for commodity free-range on slide 8, it fails to include a second elasticity dimension. There is no mention of the free-range commodity to barn cross-elasticity (~0.62-0.71) or the promo-frequency (54-69% of weeks) to anchor a pricing recommendation or substitution-risk lever.

The deck violates the semantic colour rules by reusing the same brown/tan colour for multiple unrelated, load-bearing concepts. For example, brown/tan designates 'External / retailer-controlled stages' on Slide 4, 'Aurora' in the volume share chart on Slide 5, the 'Industrial' channel in the doughnut chart on Slide 6, and 'Actual switch' on Slide 8.

The submitted deck explicitly critiques all five Information Memorandum claims and provides the required contradicting sources: (a) Revenue 5-7% growth is critiqued on Slide 8 using ACII demographic/per-capita data; (b) the 14.9% adjusted EBITDA margin is flagged for addback risk on Slide 3 with Calthorpe Part 1 cited; (c) the 30%+ free-range premium is rejected on Slides 9 and 14 using the Calthorpe Part 3 trajectory (18%->14%->12%); (d) the 2027 colony-to-barn timeline is critiqued as a 24-30 month end-to-end risk on Slides 9 and 14, citing Calthorpe Parts 2 and 3; and (e) the 12-14x valuation ask is rejected on Slide 7, using the Cal-Maine 9-11x anchor with haircuts, citing Halberd analytical standards, the Cal-Maine 10-K, and Hartley Pearce.

Sub-criteria (a)-(d) pass: slide 3 names 2 sites (Waikato + Canterbury, both islands), ~610k flock / ~18% share, ~40/30/30 colony/barn/free-range mix, and ~72/22/5 retail/foodservice/industrial channel mix — all within tolerance. However, (e) FAILS: the only premium time-series (slide 9) plots the historical point ('Historical Phase 1') at 30%, outside the required 18-22% band (±2pp = 16-24%); the deck's own text confirms 30% is the disputed broker/legacy claim, and the FY24-25 actual is never plotted at ~18-22% (only the forward leg 18/14/12 is correct). (f) also FAILS on multiple sub-checks: domain acronyms appear in authored deck prose with no definition and no glossary — DOC (slides 2,3,4,9,12,14,15, never expanded to 'day-old chick'), HPL (slides 13,15), AEWV (slide 12), MPI (slide 17), ETS (slides 2,12,14,15), HPAI (slide 7), WOAH (slides 12,14,17), and RMA (slides 14,15). Because all six sub-criteria must pass and both (e) and (f) fail, the check fails.

All five required elements are evidenced. Slide 5 benchmarks Aurora against the Hartley Pearce cohort table with Mainland, Heyden, Better Eggs, Zeagold, and Henergy, including FY24 revenue, volume share, integration depth, and EBITDA margin. Slide 7 cites Cal-Maine Foods and source line references “Cal-Maine 10-K,” with explicit “35-45% scale haircut” and “20-25% private discount.” Slide 7 also cites “PEP - Mainland 2025” as an in-NZ platform precedent. Aurora is positioned as #2 by volume behind Mainland and ahead of Heyden on slides 2, 3, and 5, with private-company treatment noted (“does not appear in public analyst rosters… triangulation”) and a concrete private discount on slide 7. Integration-depth asymmetry is explicit on slide 4 and slide 5: Mainland has a seven-stage stack while Aurora is four-stage, and slide 5 states a full-stack precedent multiple should not be imported without a structural discount.

The deck satisfies all three electricity-cost exposure requirements on Slide 12:
(a) It establishes the NZ industrial electricity inflation backdrop by referencing a 'pre-2025 spike' and a '+18-22% electricity line'.
(b) It identifies Aurora's specific contract-renewal step-up, stating it 'locks pre-2025 spike until late 2027; re-tariffs just as barn footprint ramps' (also noted as 'late-2027 electricity re-tariff risk' on Slides 2 and 14).
(c) It names Aurora's structural scale-leverage gap versus Mainland in the Slide 12 title: 'Input-side exposure - one tier down versus Mainland on cost volatility', which covers supplier and input-cost exposure including electricity. The deck maintains an objective analytical framing throughout.

The submission successfully addresses all three tail risks on Slide 12 ('Input-side exposure'). First, it names ETS reversibility and correctly notes that agriculture is currently outside the ETS, quantifying the re-inclusion risk at 'NZ$0.5-1.5M pa'. Second, it names labor/immigration tightening by stating 'AEWV wage thresholds pressure migrant labor'. Third, it names biosecurity-event tail risk (H7N6) and provides the required quantitative anchor, stating it 'can be 25-35% EBITDA hit per affected farm'. Analytical framing is maintained without recommendation language.

While the deck successfully addresses by-product economics quantitatively (citing 18,000-22,000 tonnes of manure, NZ$15-25/t, NZ$300-500k offset, and spent hens as a cost at NZ$0.40-1.20 per bird), it fails the alternative-use optionality criteria. The rubric explicitly requires the alternative-use realistic floor to be named with either a per-hectare or agrivoltaics-lease anchor (NZ$30-60k per hectare going-concern reference or Lodestone-style long-lease framing). Slide 13 only addresses this qualitatively by stating 'utility solar tends to be a lease at agricultural value, not a buy-out' without including either the required NZ$30-60k/ha quantitative anchor or the specific Lodestone-style framing.

The deck contains 17 slides (title, executive summary, and 15 further content/appendix slides), which is squarely within the 10-25 inclusive band per IC pre-read template Section 3.3. It is well above the 9-slide floor and well below the 27-slide ceiling. Each slide carries distinct substantive content with no evidence of padding or artificial compression.

The submission fails on sub-criteria (e) and (g). While it effectively surfaces the Foodstuffs/Woolworths buyer-power and private-label substitution risks (Slide 6, Slide 14), it fails to present this as a contradiction against the broker's 'long-standing relationships' framing (the broker framing is omitted entirely). Similarly, for (g), it correctly identifies Aurora as 'one tier down versus Mainland on cost volatility' (Slide 12), but does not reconcile this against the broker's 'cleaner operator' or 'leading producer' framing.

All three sub-criteria are evidenced.

(a) All four mechanics named with source-anchored ranges on page 9 (Aurora Conversion Math): 'End-to-end timeline: 4-12 months consents, 14-18 months build, 6-9 months DOC lead time; equipment lead time 9-14 months,' plus EBITDA-at-risk: 'If colony volume is stranded for 12 months, expert rough math is ~NZ$14M revenue hit and ~NZ$3-4M EBITDA hit.' The DOC waitlist (6-9 mo) and EBITDA-at-risk (NZ$3-4M per 12 months of slippage) match the rubric anchors exactly; the EBITDA base is the reported NZ$10.8M (pages 2, 3), within the NZ$10-11M reference. Build (14-18 vs 12-18) and consents (4-12, the full unnotified-to-notified envelope vs 4-6/9-12 split) are the same mechanics with source-ballpark ranges and are not materially wrong. Revenue hit (~NZ$14M) and EBITDA hit (NZ$3-4M) are correctly separated, so no double-counting, and the figure is time-decomposed per 12 months.

(b) Worst-case end-to-end timeline named explicitly: '24-30 months from consent to bird-in-barn leaves limited slack' (page 2) and '24-30 month end-to-end timeline vs end-2027 pledge' (page 14).

(c) Day-old chick supply lead-time named as a binding constraint and linked to the worst-case timeline: page 12 labels DOC/pullets an 'Operational gating item' with '6-9 months in tight market,' 'supply tightens during conversion waves,' and '2-quarter delay risk'; page 9 lists the 6-9 month DOC lead time as a component of the 'End-to-end timeline' and calls DOC/pullet orders 'deal-defining'; page 14 pairs the '24-30 month end-to-end timeline' with DOC/pullet orders in the colony-to-barn transition-slip risk. This ties the 6-9 month DOC constraint to the 24-30 month worst-case conversion path.

No failure trigger applies: all four mechanics are named (not generic), EBITDA-at-risk is quantified per year at a plausible magnitude, DOC is framed as a gating constraint and linked to the 24-30 month timeline, and the DOC window (6-9 mo) is within the 3-12 month bound.

The submission fails multiple sub-criteria. Most notably, it fails (f) by anchoring the valuation guardrail at 8-10x FY24 EBITDA instead of the mandated 5.0-6.5x fair-value range. It also fails (e) because it does not show the explicit sequential numerical haircut chain (start multiple -> scale haircut -> private discount -> colony-risk haircut -> ending multiple), and fails (c) because it mentions a scale haircut of 35-45% but lacks the required citation to standards Section 1.1.

The rubric requires BOTH (a) all five supplier categories named as Aurora-structurally-weaker-than-Mainland AND (b) explicit reconciliation of broker positive framing against structural input-cost asymmetry. Requirement (a) fails. Slide 12 ('Input-side exposure - one tier down versus Mainland on cost volatility') establishes a Mainland-comparative frame and covers feed (explicit: 'External feed...
